chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from al-Abbas ibn 'Amir, from Dawud ibn al-Husayn, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

"And the mothers shall nurse their children." He said: "As long as the child is in the period of nursing, he is equally shared between the two parents. But when he is weaned, the father has more right to him than the mother. And if the father dies, the mother has more right to him than the agnates. And if the father finds someone to nurse him for four dirhams, and the mother says, 'I will not nurse him unless for five dirhams,' then he has the right to take him from her, unless he sees that it is better for him and more gentle for him to leave him with his mother."

key_terms.يَنْزِعَهُ: to take away / to remove custody

ai.seo_question: What are the Shia jurisprudential rules for child custody after divorce and the death of a parent?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the evolving custody rights (*hadanah*) in Shia jurisprudence, emphasizing the transition from equal parental standing during nursing to paternal precedence post-weaning. It highlights the practical legal mechanism of compensation for nursing and the mother's right to retain custody if the father's offer is insufficient, provided it serves the child's best interest (*maslaha*).
